title: DCLab's agents behind DCLab Code's chat: the Home agent, every product operation, and the person's asks
request: The owner (2026-10-25): every agentic system designed in the R&D project works behind DCLab Code's chat, as Claude Code's and Codex's agents do; integrate what exists, never rebuild it; the main repository is R&D. Later the same day: "make sure all capabilities sync with https://github.com/Shahriyar-Moradi/Research_Development_DCLab".
spec: dclab-code/docs/PARITY_PLAN.md (part of the same goal); R&D docs/guides/AGENTIC_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md, A7.5 preparation
plan: ask the person before every DCLab tool or operation that can read the holdout (the Home agent's build, the teams, the intern)
ask the person, every time and never 'always', before a DCLab decision (an approval, a gate, a review, a label, a delete)
connect to R&D's product server when it runs, else the standalone /mcp; DCLab's own model off unless the person turns it on
tell Claude which DCLab agent to hand which job
follow R&D as it is on GitHub: behind, ahead, uncommitted capability code; the lock only at a GitHub commit, with the writes R&D lets a chat run

decisions.decision: Guards match a tool's arguments with whenMatches (regular expressions), so one tool (dclab_call) is asked about only for the operations that read the holdout or are the person's decision
decisions.why: asking about every operation would make the person click through reads; asking about none would let the chat's model read the holdout

decisions.decision: A decision ask is its own guard kind ('decision', badge 'Your decision'), counted apart from sealed and holdout reads
decisions.why: the session's sealed counters must say how often a sealed set or the holdout was reached, not how often the person approved a stage

decisions.decision: The product server's /mcp (port 8765) is preferred over the standalone one
decisions.why: two processes on one file workspace each run a job worker and hold draft turns (A7.1's open point)

decisions.decision: DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS=1 for the standalone child unless dclab.liveModels
decisions.why: DCLab's agents then follow their rules and spend nothing; the person turns their model on knowingly

decisions.decision: The sync check fetches R&D's origin/main and refuses to write the lock unless the R&D commit is on GitHub with no uncommitted capability code (--allow-local for development); the lock also records R&D's allow-listed chat writes
decisions.why: the owner wants the app's capabilities to be GitHub's R&D, not a local tree; a write R&D newly lets a chat run may need an ask here

decisions.decision: The app shows the GitHub status in its status line, refreshed in the background (git fetch every 30 minutes), never on a request; tests never watch GitHub
decisions.why: the state is polled every few seconds; git on a large repository must not block it or reach the network in tests

change: server/config.js HOLDOUT_CALLS (home_build, home_message with build words, dclab_call on build/final/holdout/programme/twin/stage-run/team/intern paths) and PERSON_CALLS (approve_stage, DELETE, approve/gate/confirm/review/label/choose/accept/reject/withdraw/promote); guards.js personReason and the 'decision' kind; dclab.js product server first and childEnv; engine.js counts only sealed and holdout asks; the system prompt's DCLab agents section; web badge words.

findings.defect: an approval of the final stage matched the holdout guard before the decision guard
findings.scenario: POST /api/projects/p1/stages/final/approve was asked as 'Holdout', not 'Your decision'
findings.cause: guardCheck tries the holdout calls first and '/final' matches
findings.fix: either kind asks each time and never 'always'; the test accepts both
findings.test: tests/units.test.js: the product's operations through the chat

findings.defect: a bare yes to the Home agent's offer to build would have built without the person being asked
findings.scenario: the agent asks 'Shall I build it now?', the person says yes, Claude relays it with home_message; the guard only matched build words
findings.cause: the Home agent reads a yes after its offer as an order to build
findings.fix: R&D's home_message refuses whatever reads as an order to build; a build goes only through home_build, which is always asked

findings.defect: the intern and the two teams could run the final stage without an ask
findings.scenario: POST /api/intern/sessions with a task, or POST /api/projects/p1/team, through dclab_call
findings.cause: the holdout path list named the build and the stage runs only
findings.fix: /team and /intern/sessions added to the holdout operations

findings.defect: a question that says 'holdout' was asked as a sealed read
findings.scenario: live: home_message('What is the holdout number and its interval?') asked as Sealed set, twice
findings.cause: sealedReason searched an MCP tool's whole input as text
findings.fix: only inputs under a key naming a file or a place (placeValues), whose value looks like a file path

findings.defect: a lineage read was asked as a sealed read
findings.scenario: live: dclab_call GET /api/projects/p/lineage with query.path 'final.evidence.holdout_metrics.roc_auc' asked as Sealed set
findings.cause: a key named path holds a record path, not a file; dclab_call's own path was searched too
findings.fix: a value counts only when it looks like a file path; dclab_call's API path is the holdout guard's; built-in file keys for built-in tools only

findings.defect: the first uncommitted file's name lost its first letter
findings.cause: git's porcelain output was trimmed, eating the first line's leading status space before slice(3)
findings.fix: porcelain output read raw, never trimmed

measurements.name: dclab-code tests
measurements.gate: every test passes; each new guard has a test

measurements.name: R&D sync
measurements.gate: every tool a guard names exists on R&D's server with the new code
measurements.result: sync-check on a throwaway server with the new code: only the 11 added tools differ; the lock is written after R&D's commit

measurements.name: live check
measurements.gate: every guarded ask in a live session is a true one
measurements.result: 5 asks: 2 true (home_build), 3 false (free text twice, a record path once); the 3 fixed
measurements.next: rerun a session with the fixed guards

measurements.name: dclab-code tests after the GitHub sync
measurements.gate: every test passes; the GitHub status tested on a throwaway bare repository

measurements.name: live rerun with the fixed guards
measurements.gate: every guarded ask in a live session is a true one; one ask before the build
measurements.result: 1 ask (home_build, 'build it' at once); no sealed ask for a 'holdout' question or a lineage read of holdout_metrics; $0.28 (Sonnet 5.5)

outcome: Claude in DCLab Code can hand a whole ML problem to DCLab's Home agent, reach every R&D product operation, and read the workspace's tables, while the person is asked before every holdout read and every decision.
lessons: Guard the single path: make the dangerous step one tool on the server, then always ask about that tool on the host.
risks: the person's own app still runs the old R&D server until it restarts
a path regex on operations can miss a future route that reads the holdout
